# HAZID Register — New Tank Farm, Phase 1 (Site-X)

> ⚠️ **STUDY NOT YET PERFORMED — STRUCTURED REGISTER ONLY.**
> The workshop record supplied names only two disciplines (civil engineering and operations). A HAZID requires a full multidisciplinary team — process, project/design, operations, environmental, and a chair/scribe — before its findings can stand as a completed study. This register is therefore issued as a **structured register with the supplied extract recorded**, and the study itself is marked **not yet performed**. It must be completed (or re-validated) by a reconvened full team before any design or approval decision relies on it.

## Data protection & de-identification statement

The source workshop notes were de-identified before this register was assembled. Identifiers detected and removed at source: two participant names, one telephone number, one email address, and one site address. All participants appear below as role/competency labels only. The re-identification key is held in a separate, access-controlled artifact and is **not** reproduced or referenced anywhere in this document; this register contains no name↔label mapping. Injury data in Section 8 is aggregated: no category with fewer than 5 individuals is published, and secondary suppression has been applied so suppressed cells cannot be back-calculated from the totals. Store this register apart from the re-identification key.

## 5. Risk matrix

The default 5×5 matrix with process-safety descriptors is carried as the working matrix for this register [ASSUMPTION — no company matrix was pasted into the supplied notes; confirm or substitute the site matrix before the full study]. **No line in this register has been scored against it.** Applying the matrix requires the team's likelihood and severity judgements, which were not supplied; the single recorded line therefore carries [GAP] in its risk-rank column rather than an invented score.

---

## 6. Hierarchy-of-controls review of recorded controls

Per KB-SNIP-HOC, every recorded control set is ranked against the hierarchy of controls (elimination → substitution → engineering → administrative → PPE):

| Line | Control | HoC tier | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| HAZ-01 | Bund capacity sized | Engineering | Passive engineered containment — high in the hierarchy for a loss-of-containment consequence |
| HAZ-01 | High-level alarm with automatic isolation | Engineering | Active engineered safeguard — instrumented detection with an automatic executive action, not reliant on operator response alone |

**HoC flag check:** the recorded control set for HAZ-01 is **not** administrative- or PPE-only; no lower-order-only flag is raised. Note for the reconvened team: whether elimination or substitution options (e.g. inventory reduction, tank layout) were considered upstream is [GAP] — not recorded; an early-stage HAZID is the right point to test the higher tiers before the design freezes.

## 10. Next steps to complete the study

These are facilitation actions to complete the HAZID itself — they are not hazard-register recommendations and add no hazard the team did not raise:

1. **Reconvene the full multidisciplinary team** — process, project/design, operations, environmental, plus an appointed chair and scribe. Owner: Project HSE Lead (role). Due: before the next project stage gate — [GAP: gate date not supplied].
2. **Confirm the life-cycle stage and the risk matrix**, and assemble the siting evidence pack (plot plan, siting/QRA study, met & flood data, any prior HAZID). Owner: Project Engineering Lead (role).
3. **Sweep all nine categories in session**, recording hazard → cause → consequence → existing controls → recommendation exactly as the team raises them, ranking each line on the confirmed matrix, and identifying receptors for every external/environmental line.
4. **Re-examine HAZ-01 with the full team** — establish the cause, identify receptors, score the risk, and test elimination/substitution options before confirming reliance on the engineered containment and isolation controls.
5. **SMART-validate and track every recommendation to closure** in the Section 7 tracker, each with a role owner and due date.

## Standards and knowledge base applied

- **KB-STD-IEC-61882** — structured-study discipline (HAZID shares the structured hazard-study method; applied jurisdiction-independently).
- **KB-STD-ISO14001** — environmental category framing for release-to-land/water/air hazards and receptor identification.
- **KB-SNIP-HOC** — hierarchy-of-controls ranking applied to every recorded control set (Section 6).
- Jurisdiction-specific regulatory citation: none — jurisdiction is [GAP]; to be added only after the jurisdiction (and state, where applicable) is confirmed.

---

## Limitations

This register is **decision-support only** and was produced by an assistive tool that structures and records the team's hazard identification: it contains no hazard, cause, consequence, control, or risk rank that the participants did not supply — every unsupplied item is recorded as a literal [GAP]. The study is marked **not yet performed** pending a full multidisciplinary team. This document is not a completed HAZID, not legal advice, and must be reviewed — and the study completed — under the direction of a **competent person** before any reliance is placed on it.
